newsitem.title: USA: Ben & Jerry's pulls out of Russian joint venture.
newsitem.headline: Ben & Jerry's pulls out of Russian joint venture.

text.p: Ben & Jerry's Homemade Inc has transferred its 70 percent stake in a five-year-old Russian joint venture to the city of Petrozavodsk, company officials said Thursday.

"We've been thinking of doing this for the last six months or so," Bramm Kleppner, head of the ice cream maker's Russian operations, said in a telephone interview from the company's Vermont headquarters.

He estimated that the joint venture, Iceverk, which has annual sales of less than $1 million, was worth $100,000 to $150,000, "but our ownership has been depreciated to zero on our books, so we're not going to take a hit."
Iceverk "never made a profit," he said.

"It came close to the edge a few times but never got there," Kleppner said. "It was eating up a lot of management's time...and from our point of view all the problems required more time and more resources than we could devote to it."

The transfer of the plant and store, which employs 65 people full-time, to Petrozavodsk, the capital city of Karelia that lies several hundred miles north of Moscow, was unrelated to a criminal investigation stemming from a New York businessman's allegations that Iceverk's general manager defrauded him in a joint coffee venture, Kleppner said.
